Original Owner Parked This 1964 Chevelle Malibu in Their Yard in 1987, Overheating Blamed
27 photos
Photo: eBay seller evilcotgrevil
Sitting for at least several decades. This is the sad story of the 1964 Chevrolet Chevelle Malibu that you can see in the photos. This car spent way too many years in the owner’s yard after struggling with some overheating issues.
The vehicle has obviously seen better days, and based on the photos, it’s all because of the long time of sitting. The images suggest the vehicle has been sitting under a tarp right outside in the owner’s yard, so the metal issues are barely surprising.
“The floor and the trunk pans need to be replaced,” the seller explains.
The 1964 Chevelle lineup was offered in five body styles, beginning with the Series 300 sedan, the Series 300 wagon, and continuing with the Malibu coupe and the Malibu convertible. The 1964 model year also witnessed the return of the El Camino, previously offered as a stand-alone series supposed to compete with the Ford Ranchero in 1959 and 1960, which was now the pickup version of the Chevelle.
Chevrolet tried to configure the Chevelle in such a way that it would join its portfolio right below the money-making Impala. It was offered with two six engines - a 194 and a 230 - but also borrowed some small-block engines from the Impala, including the 283 and the 327.
This Chevelle Malibu left the factory with a 283 under the hood and a two-speed Powerglide transmission. “It should be matching numbers,” the seller says, suggesting that the man who picked up the car from the dealership was his father.
It is therefore available with lots of original goodies, including the wheel covers, the bill of sale, the manuals, and the ash trays. A title is now available.
“Dad can’t find the title, so we’re going to have a new one printed on Monday, October 26,” the seller explains.
As for the reason the car ended up parked in the owner’s yard, it was all due to an overheating issue the engine suffered long ago.
“In 1987, it was overheating, and cold water was poured in. Oil started mixing with antifreeze, and it wasn’t started again,” the owner explains in the eBay listing.
Whoever buys the car will now have to check this issue, so if possible, tell your mechanic to inspect everything under the hood before making an offer.
The Chevelle is selling at no reserve for now, with a $4,000 offer currently allowing you to get your hands on the car. If you want to get this project without a fight and avoid the fierce battle that could emerge in the coming days, you can trigger the Buy It Now option and pay $5,200 for the car.
The vehicle is parked in Shepherdstown, West Virginia, and the auction is configured to end in 3 days.
Via // eBay

The 2027 Domani 311BH Is the Nicest Bunkhouse Travel Trailer Around
19 photos
Photo: YouTube/Pine Acres RV Moncton
Instead of a New Year's resolution, KZ RV kicked off the new year with a new product line, as befits any respectable RV manufacturer. The Domani line of travel trailers, described as yacht-like on the inside but more spaceship-like on the exterior, currently counts with six floorplans, including the one that's been described as the nicest bunkhouse travel trailer around.
Domani debuted in early 2026, with the first demo units for the largest and smallest floorplans arriving as 2026 model years. Right now, KZ RV is already shipping 2027 units out to dealers, which makes this as good a time as ever to discuss about the Domani gem that hardly gets any attention, though it should.
That would be the Domani 311BH, or Domani DM311BH by its full name, the bunkhouse floorplan from the series. Being a bunkhouse model makes this the most family-friendly unit as well, but don't take that to mean less style, less attention to detail, or any kind of compromise for quality.
The 311BH has sleeping for as many as eight people at once, but the high sleeping capacity doesn't come at the expense of style or comfort . Like the other Domani floorplans, this one too features interiors inspired by yacht design, with an exterior that brings to mind spaceship comparisons.
Photo: KZ RV A Domani is designed to stand out from afar, as you must know if you're familiar with these new trailers. It's painted a lighter gray with automotive paint and an automotive windshield on that distinctive front cap, and it features a lighting system that allows you to turn it into a real attention magnet at camp.
More than a looker, a Domani is designed for superior comfort, with very nice amenities. Since the debut of the Domani range in January 2026, comparisons with the Brinkley travel trailers have abounded, and not few are those who tip the scales in Domani's favor, especially if they also consider the lower price tag.
The 311BGH comes with aluminum framing and laminated Azdel composite panels, Tufflex PVC roofing, and a chassis with tandem axles and a dropped frame construction at the front. Total length is at 36 feet 10 inches (11.2 meters), and while the chassis isn't a widebody one, you still get more volume to work with at camp thanks to the single, quite large slide-out.
Photo: YouTube/Pine Acres RV Moncton It holds a pair of electric theater seats with recliner, massage, and heat functions, a residential 12V fridge, and a pantry with adjustable shelves and pull-out cubbies. Across the way, so directly to the left hand side of the main entry (this unit has two entryways, one of which gives into the main bedroom for maximum privacy and convenience), is the entertainment center.
The TV is on a televator, which allows KZ to have the living space flow organically into the kitchen, but also to offer you uninterrupted views of the campsite if you want them. A large electric fireplace and some storage is also included.
Also here is a pull-out sofa that can accommodate two more extra guests, once you extend it fully into the living room space. It comes with overhead cabinetry for storage and a large mirror that does the trick of making this space feel larger than it is.
Photo: YouTube/Pine Acres RV Moncton The mid kitchen is compact but excellently appointed, with solid surface seamless counters, soft close hinges on all opening doors, dovetail joinery on the drawers, and premium appliances. That means a three-burner gas cooktop with a large oven, a GE microwave, an extractor, and the 12V fridge some distance away. An all-accessory sink, heaps of storage space, and plenty of workspace for meal prepping are also included.
At the rear is the "BH" part of the name, the bunkhouse. Unlike with other travel trailers , it seems that KZ is striving to create a real room for the kids, a space that wouldn't feel like an afterthought or a halfway solution to them. In the 311BH, that means double-over-double bunks, each with their own windows and lights, but also a privacy door, a wardrobe, and some space for shoes before stepping into the beds.
At the other end of the trailer is the parents' bedroom, which is imagined as a private oasis with plenty of space and even more privacy. It comes standard with a king bed with heaps of storage, including in drawers under the bed, a closet with washer-dryer prep, prep for a second TV, and the aforementioned second entry.
Photo: YouTube/Pine Acres RV Moncton A second low-profile AC unit is also available here.
The only bathroom onboard is right outside the main bedroom. It might prove not enough if the trailer is at maximum capacity because people will be queuing up to use it, but once inside, it will work. Standard equipment here includes a nice walk-in one-piece fiberglass shower, a porcelain toilet, and a stainless steel sink on a vanity with integrated storage .
Designed for family use and entertaining, the DM311BH comes with an outdoor kitchen under the larger awning, with a slide-out electric griddle and a compact fridge just perfect for drinks.
Photo: YouTube/Pine Acres RV Moncton Standard features include smart power control, including for the KZ-patented four-zone lighting system, prep for solar, an on-demand tankless water heater, a 30,000-BTU furnace, two AC units, large storage compartments outside, electric auto leveling, and two LP tanks. This trailer will hold 45 gallons (170 liters) of freshwater, 76 gallons (287 liters) of gray, and 30 gallons (113 liters) more of black water.
KZ RV lists a gross weight for the 2027 Domani DM311BH of 9,800 lbs (4,445 kg) with 1,500 lbs (680 kg) of cargo, and an MSRP of $80,461. That said, the final sale price will depend on options and the dealer you're getting it from.
Photo: YouTube/Pine Acres RV Moncton Speaking of dealers, the video tour below is courtesy of a Canadian, over-enthusiastic dealer that's already made up their mind that this Domani is better than a Brinkley any time of day. But you decide that for yourself.

Restored 1966 Chevy Caprice Looks Beautiful and Needs Nothing, Don't Trust the Odometer
27 photos
Photo: Druk Auto on eBay
This Caprice isn’t a regular full-size Chevrolet . It’s a restored car that’s here because it’s ready to sell, with the dealer in charge of finding a buyer revealing that it doesn’t need anything, and it’s ready for the road.
To be honest, this is barely a surprise. The photos speak for themselves and reveal a very good-looking Caprice. The reason why everything is in such good shape is a previous restoration. That’s right, this Caprice has already been refreshed, and that is why you shouldn’t trust the odometer.
If you get inside this Caprice, you’ll discover that the car shows 13K miles on the clock, and while that wouldn’t be such a big surprise, this isn’t the actual mileage. This is because the odometer was reset when the car was restored, as the dealer explains.
The Caprice was born in 1965, when Chevrolet tried to repeat the Impala success with a similar approach. The Caprice was the top Impala version, just like the Impala was the top Bel Air version when it launched in 1958. Just like the Impala, the Caprice also needed a single year to graduate from a version of another nameplate to a stand-alone series.
Starting in 1966, the Caprice was a series of its own, and it rapidly gained ground, becoming a very solid reason to buy a full-size Chevrolet. It had all the bells and whistles you could get in a full-size Chevy, despite sharing the look and many engines with its regular siblings. The Caprice could not be ordered with a six, as it was exclusive with V8 engines.
This specimen is powered by a 327 with a four-barrel carburetor. The engine is paired with the original Powerglide automatic transmission, and considering it’s a restored car, it shouldn’t be such a big surprise that everything is running properly. The dealer describes this Caprice as “comfortable to drive,” and there’s no doubt this is true, considering the Caprice was the top full-size Chevrolet.
Born and raised in Texas, this Caprice probably never struggled with major rust problems. However, I would still raise the car on a lift and inspect the underside, especially because no information was provided on the work it received during the restoration. The dealer claims live walkarounds can also be offered via FaceTime, so you should be able to obtain more information without going there in person.
Like any other 1966 Caprice in good shape, this specimen can’t sell for beer money, though it’s not a super-expensive full-size Chevy either. The dealer wants $22,980 for this Caprice, but the Make Offer option is also available, which is typically an indication that further negotiations are also allowed.
The listing expires in 2 days, and the car is parked in Anoka, Minnesota.
Via // eBay

This Tuned Mercedes-AMG SL 63 Roadster Can Give Supercars a Run for Their Money
7 photos
Photo: Instagram | performmaster
Can you believe it’s been five years since the latest Mercedes-AMG SL premiered? The R232 debuted in October 2021, and it hit the assembly line at the Bremen factory in Germany in March 2022.
Unlike its predecessors, it comes exclusively as an AMG, and it is a 2+2 roadster with a two-door configuration. Well, unless we are talking about the Maybach version, because this one has seating for only two. Depending on the configuration, you can get the new-gen SL either with rear-wheel drive or 4Matic+ all-wheel drive, and all versions are based on the MSA platform, just like the modern-day GT (2-door).
Mercedes- AMG ’s modern-day SL is definitely a head-turner, this writer believes, but it is also one pricey cookie. For the base SL 43 , you know, the one with the four-banger, which has 416 horsepower on tap and hits 60 mph (97 kph) in 4.6 seconds, you will have to fork out a minimum of $114,900 for the latest model year in the United States of America, and that’s before factoring in the destination charge, options, and dealer fees.
The V8-powered SL 55, which has 469 hp and reaches 60 mph in 3.8 seconds, you’d better prepare at least $147,750. The SL 63 also packs a V8, albeit one with 577 hp, is three-tenths of a second faster than the SL 55, and starts at $190,500. The PHEV SL 63 S E Performance has 805 hp in total, hits 60 mph in 2.8 seconds, and kicks off at $207,900. And the Mercedes-Maybach SL Roadster can be had from $225,900, has the same engine as the SL 63, and needs 4.0 seconds to reach 60 mph from rest.
Photo: Instagram | performmaster Now, there are plenty of tuning upgrades for the entire modern-day Mercedes-AMG SL family, as well as the Mercedes-Maybach SL 680 Monogram Series , regardless of whether you want your roadster to have more power, a dedicated body kit, new wheels, a custom interior, and so on. And one of the companies that ticks some of these boxes is PerformMaster. You do remember this tuner, don’t you? You should, because it does not step over the line, as its builds are always on the cool side of things.
But does this also apply to the pictured ride? Why, of course it does. This is a Mercedes-AMG SL 63, which features a turbo upgrade from the quoted tuner, and a PEC Performance System, the company says. Do you know how much it has on tap? That would be 794 hp (805 ps/592 kW) and 719 pound-feet (975 Nm) of torque. According to PerformMaster, the 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 kph) acceleration takes just 3.0 seconds, and that is on par with previous generation supercars.
By comparison, the Lamborghini Huracan Evo Spyder is actually one-tenth of a second slower, as it takes 3.1 seconds to zip from 0-62 mph, and will do 202 mph (325 kph) flat-out. The 5.2-liter naturally aspirated V10 engine produces 631 horsepower (640 ps/470 kW) and 443 lb-ft (600 Nm) of torque in the demised open-top supercar, in case you forgot.
Despite the impressive power boost, this tuned SL 63 is still no match for the Mercedes-AMG SL 63 S E Performance. That’s because the electrified model can reach 62 mph in just 2.8 seconds, two-tenths of a second faster, and has 805 hp (816 ps/601 kW) and 1,048 lb-ft (1,420 Nm) of torque to play with. Not bad at all for something like this, is it?
Photo: Instagram | performmaster One might think that besides the power boost, PerformMaster must have done something else to the pictured Mercedes-AMG SL . But that’s not the case, because everything you see here, from the front bumper, Panamericana grille, hood, door mirror casings, and side skirts, to the rear bumper, and diffuser have come directly from the factory. Thus, noting gives it away, not even on the inside, because the cockpit hasn’t been touched with the tuning stick either.
According to PerformMaster, the oily upgrades are accompanied by a vehicle-specific TUV certificate, as well as its own engine warranty, which is up to 24 months or 100,000 kilometers (62,137 miles) for extra peace of mind. Thus, if you want to make your SL 63 more powerful, and these numbers sound perfect, then you may want to reach out to the tuner to discuss the details, including the pricing, because these haven’t been released at the time of writing.
This is definitely my kind of tuning job, as it makes the entire thing a heck of a lot more appealing, and it proves that most cars do no need wacky updates inside and out to stand out more, as a power boost is easily does the trick. But if you had an SL 63 in your garage and wanted to make it a bit cooler, would you opt for this oily upgrade? View this post on Instagram A post shared by performmaster (@performmaster)

Would You Make Your BMW X6 M Look Like This?
10 photos
Photo: Instagram | revozport
Unlike its more practical (and better looking, this writer thinks) sibling, the X5, which has been replaced by a new generation , the BMW X6 is here to stay, for now anyway, because its replacement is reportedly due some two years from now, probably debuting in late 2028, and hitting dealers nationwide for the 2029 model year.
By then, the current third-gen will be more than nine years old, as the assembly commenced back in August 2019. The G06 is based on the CLAR platform, just like the older X5, the previous 7 Series, 8 Series, first-gen X7, and the controversial XM. Its successor, on the other hand, will build on an updated version of the same construction. How do we know that? Because so does the new-age X5, and the future X6 will follow in its footsteps.
Besides the architecture, we also know what it will look like, even if BMW is pretty much delaying the inevitable, because it will step into the Neue Klasse era. This means a vizor-like face similar, or perhaps identical, to that of the new BMW X5 , albeit with a sloping roofline, less space in the trunk, and less headroom for backseat occupants. The cockpit will also be identical, so if you want to see what the interior of the future X6 will look like, then look at the X5’s. Or the 3er, i3, iX3, and so on.
With this information off our chest, let’s move on to the pictured BMW X6 M, which is the real reason behind this story. Images of it were shared on social media by RevoZport earlier this week, with the tuner stating that the vehicle in question wears its “street kit.” And if that sounds familiar, then you have likely seen our coverage of the F95 BMW X5 M , which is also equipped with the tuner’s “street kit.”
Photo: Instagram | revozport Just like its more practical sibling, this BMW X6 M features the same goodies, more or less. The less part includes the hood, which hasn’t been changed. The apron, on the other hand, is new, and so is the kidney grille surround, from what we can tell. Further back, the premium mid-size super crossover coupe, or the SAV (Sports Activity Vehicle), as BMW likes to call it, features new side skirt attachments, and the door mirror casings carry over from the factory.
At the rear, the BMW X6 M in question has a much more pronounced ducktail spoiler. The multi-fin diffuser is part of the makeover, and the extras have been crafted from carbon fiber. The car has a gray look on the outside, rides on familiar wheels, and the add-ons have a forged carbon look that may sound like a bit too much, though it is not that flashy in reality, and we reckon other tuners (ahem, Mansory!) could learn a thing or two from RevoZport when it comes to this part, and not only.
The tinted windows, including the windshield, which features UV protection from what we can see, prevent us from catching a glimpse of the interior. Thus, we can assume that the upholstery and trim carry over from the factory, and this likely applies to the seats, steering wheel, door sills, and so on. What we are saying is that the cabin likely remains bone stock, and it’s up to you to decide whether that is a good or a bad thing.
Photo: Instagram | revozport We cannot end this story without mentioning the powertrain, and as you likely know, the F96-generation of the BMW X6 M features the company’s familiar V8 engine. It is a twin-turbocharged lump, which produces the exact same output and thrust as the one powering the F95 BMW X5 M. This means 617 brake horsepower, which translates to 625 metric horsepower and 460 kilowatts, with the peak output available at 6,000 rpm.
As for the thrust, it is available between 1,800 rpm and 4,600 rpm, and it is officially rated at 553 pound-feet (750 Nm) of torque. The BMW X6 M features a rear-biased xDrive all-wheel drive system, and an eight-speed automatic transmission channeling the power to both axles. It also has mild-hybrid assistance, and takes only 3.9 seconds to hit 62 mph (100 kph) from a standstill. That’s identical to the era’s X5 M, and one-tenth of a second faster than the pre-facelifted iteration.
A brand new BMW X6 M will set you back a minimum of $136,100 in the United States of America for the latest model year. That is the official MSRP as the brand’s website reveals, and it obviously excludes destination, as well as options, and dealer fees. The old BMW X5 M is still listed on the website, and it is accompanied by an MSRP of $131,000.
Now, if you owned a BMW X6 M and came across RevoZport’s pictured tuning package, would you say yes or no to it? View this post on Instagram A post shared by RevoZport (@revozportt)

Despite decades of market dominance, it seems like the days of loud, finicky, gas-powered mowers may finally be behind us; and I say that because – for the second year in a row ! – the highest-rated lawnmowers on Amazon won’t burn a drop of gas.
The latest round of dumb oil wars are ratcheting up fuel prices everywhere while, at the same time, state and local governments continue to tightening restrictions on noise and small-engine emissions . Combined, those things probably mean that your next lawn mower is more likely to plug in than fill up, whether you like it or not. The good news is that. in addition to being quieter, safer, and not poisoning the air you breathe while you walk behind them , electric laenmowers have come a long way in terms of power and performance in just a few years. So much so, in fact, that many of the highest-rated models on Amazon, emphatic period , are electric.
In putting this list together, we looked at the average star ratings of a number of lawn mowers on Amazon, focusing on products that had at least 2,000 reviews and a four-star average or higher, and found that (like last year) battery-electric units from EGO Power, Greenworks, and Worx were among the top-rated mowers, regardless of fuel type.
Here’s the rundown, in alphabetical order (by brand).
Advertisement - scroll for more content
EGO
EGO POWER+ LM2112 21″ electric mower.
Over the past few years, the EGO POWER+ brand has staked a claim to being the gold standard for cordless lawn equipment, thanks to its high-voltage 56V battery platform and premium build quality. The brand’s 21″ POWER+ LM2112 push mower currently carries a 4.5-star average rating from more than 2,200 Amazon reviews and an “Overall Pick” designation .
That’s no surprise, given the LM2112’s 6 ft-lbs. of cutting torque (equivalent to a 150cc ICE), and up to 35 minutes of runtime (call it a suburban yard) from the included 56V 4.0 Ah li-ion battery , three-in-one mulching, bagging and side-discharge capability. It also starts at the push of a button, folds for compact storage and skips the exhaust, maintenance, and oil changes that come along with a comparable gas mower.
Greenworks
Greenworks 40V 16″ push mower.
With an impressive 4.2-star rating after more than 12,000 verified reviews, the Greenworks 40V 16″ push mower is in rare company among mowers of any kind on Amazon . No surprise, given that the lightweight, cordless mower weighs just 37.5 lbs. and comes with a 4.0Ah battery and charger good for up to 40 minutes of runtime, making it ideal for homeowners with smaller yards who want to ditch gas without wrestling with a heavier machine.
The Greenpower’s 16″ cutting deck is designed for (if not limited to) compact lawns, with a five-position height adjustment and a two-in-one system offering you a choice of mulching (yes) or bagging (no) your lawn clippings.
For bigger, more demanding lawns, Greenworks offers a 4.4-star push mower with a 21″ steel cutting deck that’s powered by an 80V brushless motor and ships with a pair of 2.0 Ah batteries good for up to 40 minutes of runtime with both batteries . Three-in-one functionality for mulching, bagging, or side discharge is included, too, along with push-button starting, seven-position height adjustment, and a rapid charger that can get it back to work in about 30 minutes.
WORX
WORX 17″ battery-powered mower.
WORX’s 40V 17″ Power Share mower is another strong example of how electric lawn care can be both practical and affordable. The WG743 mates a pair of 20V, 4.0 Ah batteries to deliver 40V of power , and those same batteries work across the brand’s broader Power Share lineup of tools – a lineup that includes string trimmers, power drills, and more.
The WORX mower’s standout feature, though, is its “IntelliCut” technology that works a bit like traction control in your car, automatically increasing torque when the mower hits thicker grass (more traction) and backing off when it doesn’t need the extra power (when it detects wheelspin – or, in this case, cutting head spin). Factor in an intentionally lightweight design, seven-position cutting-height adjustment, and the de rigueur options for mulching or bagging, and you’ve got a versatile little mower for keeping a smaller lawn in shape.

1967 Chevrolet Corvette With 3,304 Miles on the Clock Rocks Tuxedo Black Look and 427ci Big Block V8
74 photos
Photo: Motorcar Classics
New York-based Motorcar Classics probably thinks it has you covered if you're willing to write a very fat check for this magnificent ‘Triple Black’ BBC (big block) V8 Chevy Corvette from 1967.
The C8 iteration of ‘America’s sports car’ is quite far and away from the humble beginnings in 1953 when the original fiberglass Corvette was almost killed before it could properly take off because of slow sales. Now, the C8 is an established legend, more than 70 years after it was first conceived.
But it’s also not very accessible anymore. Indeed, after inflation and other hikes, the 2027 Chevrolet Corvette Stingray currently kicks off at no less than $71,300 sans destination for the base Coupe version. It’s a mid-engine sports car now, indeed, and also has a brand-new 6.7-liter V8 engine rocking 535 hp and 520 lb-ft of torque, which is way more power than a base Corvette used to have back in the days of the C1.
The new engine is shared across the range with the returning Corvette Grand Sport ($86,300) and the all-new, first-ever Corvette Grand Sport X ($110k), which has come to replace the previous E-Ray as the ‘base’ performance hybrid model with all-wheel drive. Its potential? No less than 721 combined horsepower, by the way! Do you want a more expensive Corvette or power of hypercar magnitude? No problem, as the 670-hp homologation Z06 starts from almost $122k, while the Corvette ZR1 and ZR1X (hybrid) have no less than 1,064 hp and 1,250 combined hp, respectively.
Photo: Motorcar Classics Of course, they’re also more expensive: $198k and $227,800 – which is a lot of cash for a Chevrolet, for sure. But since they can go head-to-head and toe-to-toe with the likes of Ferrari, Lamborghini, or McLaren, it’s a small price to pay, right? Well, if you have reached that conclusion – that we only live once and it doesn’t kill you to spend six-figure sums on a Corvette, here’s another proposal: a 1967 Chevrolet Corvette.
Bear with us. This one is for collectors and enthusiasts alike, as it represents the final year of the C2 Corvette, the car that completely rethought the series into the model that was loved for decades until the C8 again rewrote the rule book with a mid-engine configuration. The dealership says this is a “magnificent 1967 Chevrolet Corvette Coupe representing the holy grail of American muscle and the absolute peak of second-generation Sting Ray design.”
It is finished in the desirable and factory-correct Tuxedo Black (Paint Code 900) over Black Leather upholstery (Trim Code 402); it is also contrasted with a striking Red Stinger hood, and the rare "Triple Black" big-block coupe also has the fancy chrome side exhaust “loudspeakers” along with the amplifier to make them rumble – a matching-numbers 427 cubic-inch L71 big-block V8 engine, factory-rated at ‘just’ 435 horsepower and 460 lb-ft of torque.
Photo: Motorcar Classics The engine is packing the iconic “Tri-Power” setup featuring three two-barrel Holley carburetors atop an aluminum intake manifold and is also paired with a four-speed manual transmission, so “this Corvette delivers visceral performance amplified by factory side-exit exhaust pipes with original-style heat shields and transistor ignition.” The car has gone through a “labor-intensive frame-off restoration reportedly requiring more than 2,200 man-hours and over $70,000 in parts and materials.” Cool, right?
Additionally, the chassis features power-assisted four-wheel disc brakes, power steering, and an independent rear suspension with a transverse leaf spring, plus a Positraction 3.70 ratio AO rear axle, and the car sits on beautiful, classic 15-inch turbine-style wheels wrapped in BFGoodrich Silvertown radial tires with fancy red lines, “striking the perfect balance between original aesthetics and modern drivability.”
It’s going to be a show offering, as the company explains that “every detail was meticulously addressed to meet stringent judging standards, down to correct head markings on the hardware throughout the vehicle and an undercarriage that remains as immaculate as the exterior.” It has already received multiple NCRS Top Flight awards, so the C2 with its original L71 427/435 HP engine is not only dressed to impress but also ready to roll on the show floor.
Photo: Motorcar Classics There are also a bevy of options on board, like the power steering, power brakes, power windows, tinted glass, and a vertical push-button AM/FM radio. The sale comes with “a rich documentation package, including a photocopy of the original factory tank sticker, the original Protect-O-Plate, manufacturer's literature, a reproduction window sticker, dynamic dyno test results, and official NCRS judging sheets,” among other things.
Of course, this “turnkey crown jewel ready for high-level concours display or private collection preservation” is not selling cheap: the dealership has a stated price of $289,900, but you can still negotiate through the ‘make an offer’ button on their online sales portal. So, what do you think – yay or nay? Would you buy somethign like this or a brand-new ZR1X with this kind of money?
Via // Motorcar Classics

Young Man Builds Insane Chevy C10 Truck in His Driveway: It Packs V8 Punch and 600 Horsepower
21 photos
Photo: Autotopia LA | YouTube
Roman is 25, and he has spent the past few years working on his 1971 Chevrolet C10 right in his driveway and then racing it. The street-legal, ferocious autocross machine now hits the streets and the track, pushed forward by a completely rebuilt V8 engine, with the force of 600 horsepower.
Roman is less than half the age of his street and track companion that he rebuilt from the ground up. He did most part of the job right in his driveway, not a shop, not a garage , with no lift at hand, just jacks that made enough room for him to get underneath and work. He is definitely an old soul who treasures retro styling as much as he loves autocross.
It looks like, after 55 years on and off the road, the Chevy C10 finally got in the right hands. Those of a young man who knows exactly what it can do with a bit of a power bump. Or more than a bit. The first owner of the C10 was a farm truck guy who used it as a workhorse. The second owner bought it for his son. Roman bought it from him and slowly but surely turned it into a race truck.
He built it with purpose. Everything has a function, it’s not all show and no go. It’s got no AC, but comfort wasn't exactly a top priority for him. Instead, fun was. Loud was. Performance was. He didn't build it to take it to car shows and brag about it. He built it to take it to the track and win.
Photo: 1971 Chevrolet C10 A fully built 383-cubic-inch small-block V8 sits under the hood. Roman retained the original engine block. He originally planned to swap it for a 440, but changed his mind and just rebuilt the 383 and made it run on high-octane 101 race gas. A Tremec TKX five-speed transmission puts the power down through the rear wheels.
From farm workhorse to track machine Now it makes over 600 horsepower and 600 pound-feet of torque. A Black Widow exhaust , coming out through the side, roars out the drama of the V8 from under the hood. The power plant was outfitted with a high-performance FiTech EFI setup, which Roman credits for providing razor-sharp throttle response and reliable drivability whether he's cruising on the highway or carving corners at the track.
He is still considering an upgrade to the suspension , currently featuring Viking Performance components, but he has to come up with the right setup. A specialized Nine Lives Racing frame-mounted rear wing showed up at the back to add crucial downforce over the rear tires. A McLeod clutch helps him when he wants to smoke the tires. He was after fun and wanted a truck that he could beat on. He doesn’t want to have to baby the truck.
Photo: 1971 Chevrolet C10 The truck is sitting on a Currie 9-inch, which serves as the bulletproof backbone of this build. It effortlessly absorbs aggressive downshifts, hard clutch drops, and heavy corner-exit acceleration without flexing or breaking a sweat under track conditions. Roman relocated the fuel tank to the back for improved weight distribution.
Roman runs a high-performance Wilwood disc brake setup to safely and consistently slow his good, old 1971 Chevrolet C10 down during high-speed autocross runs or whenever he wants to show off on the highway.
Less is more when you're after fun The cabin is simple and focused on performance, because sometimes, less is more. The driver and passenger sit in RaceQuip fixed-back racing seats. It is not exactly the most comfortable sitting choice, but Roman chose them for the enhanced racing feel that he gets on board. He never wanted to build a lounge on wheels. Those seats make perfect sense in a truck that spends more time at the track than it does on the road.
The driver holds a Cannonball Performance steering wheel and gets all the relevant driving data on the aftermarket digital and LED Intellitronix gauge cluster, with a classic yet sporty appearance. That is what the truck's creator wanted in the first place.
Photo: 1971 Chevrolet C10 Roman retained the original door panels, along with the door hinges and window cranks, but came up with a Level 7 pedal assembly. Roman made efforts to keep the truck looking as vintage as possible so that he would not alter its DNA.
On the road, the driveway-built Chevy C10 is stiff, light, and bad-mannered when you step on it. It can smoke tires until tomorrow (and until it runs out of rubber, of course), and it can make other motorists scratch their heads in surprise at the stoplight.
Looking all beat-up and run-down, nobody would expect it to launch like a rocket. Roman hasn't fixed the paint imperfections and isn’t planning to do it. Told you he's an old soul and patina works for him.

23 New Hot Wheels Collectibles That Are Coming to a Store Near You
37 photos
Photo: Lamley Group
Most of my friends typically spend most of their non-essential budget on shoes, gadgets, alcohol, or weekend-long trips to different countries. I’ve never cared much about shoes, have most of the gadgets I wanted in the first place, only drink alcohol regularly, and have already visited over 30 countries in 30 years.
I still engage in plenty of window shopping, looking for my next motorcycle, car and parts for my RX-7. However, all those only require part of my time for now, as my current budget is now tied up with other priorities.
That means I only spend money on purchasing new scale model cars, and one of my local shops is currently running a 30% off on select Hot Wheels vehicles. I already missed out on the '89 Mercedes-Benz 560 SEC AMG due to constantly postponing the purchase.
I might as well dive in and secure the white Ferrari 250 GTO and a few other Premium collectibles I plan to use for my future unboxing stories.
That’s a topic for another time though, as right now I just want to get you up to speed with the new Hot Wheels collectibles that are coming to a store near you. Let’s get to it!
Multipack Exclusives Photo: Hot Wheels Malaysia I’ve got three Multipack exclusive items here, and the McLaren P1 is definitely the “fastest” one. I still haven’t seen Ronald Wong’s new P1 GTR casting anywhere in the wild yet, but I can assure you Ryu Asada’s “basic” design is pretty cool too.
Given it has been around since the 2015 HW Workshop: HW Garage mini-series, I have bought and unboxed several variations (at least in the first few years of its “career”). It was part of last year’s Hybrid Energy Silver Series set, but it has been a common sight across various multipacks. I’m a fan of the new color, but would definitely paint the wheels white.
Despite its real world status, this collectible won’t be as desirable as the Porsche 934 Turbo RSR. Sure, this model might not be as popular as it was six to seven years ago. However, it feels to get another shot at it, as it was MIA both this year and in 2024. That Motul decal is bound to increase its appeal, just like the Michelin one on the Nissan Patrol Custom from next year’s Case C will.
Bryan Zhao’s BMW 635 Csi was off to a great start in last year’s Wild Widebody mini-collection, but sort of went downhill from there. I’m aware Mattel can’t give us an accurate replica of the Jagermeister livery, but that also means collectors who are looking for authenticity won’t bother buying it in the first place. Since I’ve began paying more attention to cleaner cars, I think this new variation will be the best one yet.
Tooned F1 Photo: Hot Wheels Malaysia Believe me, I am shocked about this set as you are. It was obvious the manufacturer would double down on its efforts to deliver more F1-inspired collectibles, but I did not imagine they’d go for this approach as well. Fraser Campbell designed this squished version of a 2026, generic F1 machine, and they’re obviously all the same casting.
It’s the same approach that we’ve seen for the Mainline series, where a different livery will lead the way without any chassis adjustments. While we’re used to seeing sets of five cars, you may have noticed Racing Culture and Team Transport have shifted towards four per mix and it’s the same for Tooned F1 .
Given that there are only 11 teams on the grid, I imagine each new mix will have a repeat item. That means we’ll be getting four of them throughout the year, at least if the first one performs according to plan. Right off the bat, I expect Scuderia Ferrari HP to be the first one to vanish from the pegs, despite the team’s lack of results in recent decades.
Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team will probably come in P2, with Oracle Red Bull Racing and Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team in last. Of course, I might be wrong as the hype could ensure people will just buy the entire set thinking it will be worth more later down the road. Time will tell.
Neon Speeders Photo: Hot Wheels Malaysia Neon Speeders is entering its fifth year and I’m honestly surprised it made it this far. I recently pre-ordered MiniGT’s glowing version of Rexy and I just know it will be good. The only problem is that it cost me as much as 10 Neon Speeders collectibles, but I’ve long decided to go for quality over quantity. There are only two European cars in Mix 1, and they’re part of the same family if you think about it.
Jun Imai’s Volkswagen T2 Pickup is first in line (#1 of 8) and I like everything about it except for the “mandatory” NS6 wheels. If you’d rather go for the Spectraflame look, there are two previous variations of if to look for. The Porsche 917 LH is the other Euro car in the mix, and it too showed up in The Hot Ones before: earlier this year in Spectraflame Apple Green and in 2025 in Spectraflame Gold.
I think it’s time this race car got a new casting, too, just so it can be on the same page with the Porsche 917K. Moving over to Japan, we have three items on the list. Both the Honda S800 Racing and the Nissan Skyline H/T 2000GT-X feel like ancient history. And I’m honestly surprised to get another Miata as last year’s Mix 2 featured the 2004 Mazda Mazdaspeed Miata.
The ‘91 has had a few good moments so far, including its Modern Classics variation and the Japanese Car Culture Themed Multipack model I unboxed not long ago. As we head on over to the USA, we’re also going on a trip down memory lane to the late ‘60s and early ‘70s. The '71 Dodge Charger is the interesting option in my case, and I will most definitely skip the pink Javelin and the green Corvette.
Team Transport Photo: Lamley Group Let’s discuss the Premium part of today’s list, starting with Team Transport . We already knew about Mix 1 and Mix 2 for next year, and I already want a closer look at the 1985 Chevrolet Camaro IROC-Z and the 1964 Shelby Cobra Daytona Coupe. While I’m at it, I might as well go for the Dodge/Plymouth and Porsche/Porsche combo from Mix 2: 2027 is shaping up to be an exciting year for the hobby!
The Lamley Group recently posted a sneak peak preview of what coming up after those two mixes, and I haven’t seen photos of these models anywhere else yet. While I ignored the First Edition release of the 1964 Shelby Cobra Daytona Coupe, this new IWC-themed livery is quite spectacular (and nostalgic) and the matching-colored trailer is my only complaint. The Rally Hauler is definitely turning up the heat for its seventh variation, even though it’s rolling on the same 8-spoke wheels as always.
The Honda S2000 will be my priority though, as I’ve never seen a more spectacular take on Ryu Asada’s casting. Mixing in that carbon fiber finish with he orange paint job and the Enkei-inspired wheels makes for an impressive result and I want it asap. Even the Aero Lift feels exciting as painted wheels are becoming standard in Team Transport. I’m not that interested in the all-American Team in this mix, mainly because of the hauler.
Also, one variation of the '69 Ford Torino Talladega is enough for me, thank you very much! The Porsche 917K is back for its second iteration ever, sporting an iconic blue and white paintjob. I just received my First Edition release a little while ago, so I’ll refrain from saying anything about it until I take it out of the blister card. Wouldn’t it have been amazing if it had the same opening feature as the Mazda 787B does? I still have more Hot Wheels news to share, and I’ll be back with the info soon!

2026 Paris Motor Show • OMODA 4 Lands in Paris To Showcase Futuristic Styling, Looks Like a Discount Urus
Modified F82 BMW M4 Is Now a Track-Ready Missile, Lowered, Enhanced, and Ready for Body Hugging
9 photos
Photo: Garage Kept Motors / Instagram
Sitting proudly in the inventory of Grand Rapids, Michigan-based Garage Kept Motors , this 2015 BMW M4 has the 3.0L Twin Turbo inline-six ready to fight any opponent at the owner’s favorite weekend track events.
The premium Bavarian automaker from Germany, BMW , is currently in the midst of morphing all of its models according to the Neue Klasse lifestyle, which includes a new design outside and inside plus a dedicated platform for the EV models. But not everyone is happy with the styling, as always, given some of the controversial traits, like the BMW Panoramic Vision or the kidney grille treatment, among others.
No worries, not even the current models have received unanimous praise, as many of them, the BMW M4 included, have received contentious traits, like the humongous air intakes of the G82/83 iteration. Well, on this occasion, you’re safe, as this used 2015 BMW M4 is of the tamer F82 variety, and it’s also intended for track use, meaning you can escape discussions in a safe and performance-oriented manner by saying that you’re focused on the weekend track days rather than (BMW’s) current politics.
The high-performance coupe version of the BMW 4 Series, the BMW M4 in the F82 iteration , has the S55 twin-turbocharged inline-six 3.0L engine under the hood, and this particular example is said to churn out 425 horsepower and 406 lb-ft of torque as per the factory rating. It’s also paired with the quick-shifting 7-speed dual-clutch transmission, and the white and black example has 44,418 miles on the odometer.
Alas, this Alpine White over Black BMW M4 has given those miles a run for their money, as it has “been extensively modified with a clear focus on track performance”; the suspension has Eibach race springs, Ground Control camber/caster plates, and Hotchkis race anti-sway bars and control arms. The braking performance comes courtesy of AP Racing Competition and StopTech braided SST brake lines, while Apex SM-10 wheels provide a lightweight and motorsport-inspired setup for the “square tire” goodies.
The latter include 275-width Nitto NT01 tires on all wheels, and inside the BMW M4 comes with additional track-focused equipment: a StudioRSR Tesseract roll cage, OMP WRC racing seats, and Sabelt 5-point racing harnesses. The carbon-fiber roof reduces weight and lowers the center of gravity, and the whole ride now sits closer to the ground thanks to all the other enhancements.
“This augmented F82 is ready to get back on the track with a new owner behind the wheel,” says the description from the dealership, but not before we also hear about the S55 powertrain’s performance-oriented upgrades: a Turner X-pipe with a catalytic converter delete and a Turner high-kick carbon-fiber rear spoiler.
“With its low 44,418-mile showing, Alpine White exterior, carbon-fiber roof, 7-speed DCT, and extensive collection of track-focused upgrades, this 2015 BMW M4 offers a compelling combination of modern BMW performance and motorsport-inspired hardware,” says the conclusion. But are you ready for the pricing details? Well, it turns out that this modded BMW M4 is offered at $46,900, which isn’t bad for the bundle of upgrades.
So, what do you think – yay or nay? After all, a brand-new BMW M4 Coupe starts from at least at $82,200 sans destination and potential dealer hikes. Even the entry-level BMW M2 is now $69,500, while the M3 sedan is only slightly cheaper than an M4 starting at over $79k.

2026 Paris Motor Show • Hyundai Tucson N Line Steals the Spotlight in Paris, but It's All Show and No Go
Chinese Automaker Chery Looking Into Canadian Vehicle Assembly Plant
7 photos
Photo: Chery
Looking at the bigger picture, an idle Canadian auto plant makes a lot more sense to a Chinese automaker than a shiny new factory. The folks at Chery are currently looking at ways to assemble vehicles in Canada, with executive vice president Guibing Zhang confirming that existing production capacity is what Chery is after.
Speaking to Bloomberg, the VP also made it clear that partnerships with local investors are on the menu as well. While Chery has yet to name a partner or site, the idea presented by Zhang appears to be more than a vague intention to expand overseas. And truth be told, localization would make a world of difference over Chinese rivals that have no such ambitions in North America.
Chery will enter the Canadian market in 2027, likely with the Omoda and Jaecoo brands. Extremely popular in the Old Continent, said marques racked up a great deal of registrations in September 2026. For example, the Omoda 5 moved 8,396 units in the European market, putting it 43rd between the Skoda Enyaq and Kamiq. The Jaecoo 7 is 10th overall, having sold 15,470 units last month.
Starting with imported vehicles in Canada would let Chery test demand for more affordable and well-equipped Chinese models before committing to manufacturing. Even so, Chery needs local partners to establish a proper dealership and servicing network. Canada has also changed the game for Chinese models, especially if we're talking about battery-electric models.
Back in January, an agreement reached with Beijing created a quota system that allows manufacturers to bring in 49,000 Chinese electric vehicles under a most favored nation tariff of 6.1 percent. The quota system, which increases each year by 6.5 percent, replaces the additional 100 percent surtax from before. With increasingly more Chinese BEVs allowed on an annual basis, it goes without saying that Chinese brands are rubbing their hands now.
Photo: Chery Upgrading to a Canadian factory would give Chery a long-term presence, one that would involve Canadian suppliers and partners. Zhang's position is that Canada makes sense even if Chery never gets the okay to enter the US market, and he's on to something here. Trump has already shown openness to Chinese vehicle assembly plants in the United States, but only if they employ local workers.
Chery and plenty others are still looking for a way into the United States of America, partly because it's far more lucrative than Canada. As far as we know, Chery remains open to partnerships with American automakers. The one that comes to mind is Stellantis, whose European division already builds Chinese models for the Leapmotor brand in Spain .
Ottawa has already encouraged discussions with a variety of Chinese automakers, including Chery. It, BYD, and Geely are all interested in exploring joint ventures on Canadian soil. Executive vice president Guibing Zhang indicated that Chery would also consider investment from multiple parties rather than financing the whole Canadian operation itself.
Regardless of option, every single one of them would bring its own commitments and costs. An idled plant avoids the expense and lead time of constructing a new one, but Chery would still have to make everything fit its intended vehicles and the market as a whole.
BYD, meanwhile, has already inquired about the idled Stellantis plant in Brampton, Ontario. Geely is also starting Canadian sales in 2027, but as opposed to BYD and Chery, it still hasn't announced whether local production may be in the offing.
